image_description: A close-up underwater shot of a lionfish (Pterois) swimming against a blurred rocky reef background. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical stripes, large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays, and prominent dorsal spines fanning out from its back. The head is visible on the right side with a distinct eye and mouth structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large head with prominent eyes and wide mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible on the right; the eye is distinct and the mouth structure appears consistent with scorpaenid morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a laterally compressed fish, viewed from the side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brightly striped coloration in red, white, brown, or black bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct vertical reddish-brown and white stripes are clearly visible across the body and fins.
Resolution and lighting conditions make it impossible to definitively verify the presence of individual small scales; the texture appears smooth due to image compression/quality.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal fin with numerous elongated venomous spines that fan outward like mane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal spines are clearly visible, elongated, and separated, fanning out from the dorsal ridge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are large, spread wide, and show distinct, separate elongated rays typical of lionfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Lower fins (pelvic area) are visible beneath the body with elongated spine-like structures.

artifact_observations.location: Pectoral fin tips and background interface
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the very tips of the finest pectoral rays where they meet the background, suggesting minor generation smoothing or depth-of-field simulation artifacts, but structurally coherent.
Some of the thinner dorsal spines appear to merge slightly at the base into the skin rather than having distinct insertion points, a common minor artifact in fin generation.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification of species identity and stripe pattern consistency against ImageNet classes.
Audit the connectivity of the numerous thin fin rays to ensure they don't fuse or float independently.
Verify the spatial separation of the dorsal spines from the background and each other to detect melting.
Holistic check for water distortion artifacts, unnatural lighting, or texture smearing.

focus_areas: Connectivity of pectoral fin rays to the body
Consistency of stripe patterns across body curvature
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the pectoral fin rays; AI often blurs these into the background. Verify if the dorsal spines have valid insertion points on the spine or if they appear to float above the skin. Check if the 'scales' checkpoint was unfairly marked untestable given the resolution.
